levels.title: GATE 01 — FIRST CONTACT
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

Welcome, recruit. Before you can fight NEXUS, you need to understand your weapon. JavaScript runs in every browser on the planet — it is the only language that needs no installation, no compiler, and no setup. It just runs. NEXUS knows this. So do we. Prove you understand what JavaScript is and what it can do.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. Write a JavaScript statement that displays the message "CIPHER ONLINE" in the browser console.
2. Write one that changes the text of an HTML element with the id "status" to "SYSTEMS ACTIVE".
hints: console.log("message") outputs to the browser console
document.getElementById("id").innerHTML = "text" changes page content
JavaScript is case sensitive — Console.log will not work

levels.title: GATE 02 — DEPLOYMENT POINT
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

Your code needs to be deployed correctly or it will never execute. NEXUS is counting on you placing your script in the wrong location so it runs before the page loads — crashing on empty elements. There are three places JavaScript can live: inside a <script> tag in the head, inside a <script> tag at the bottom of body, or in an external .js file. Know the difference. Deploy correctly.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. Create a variable `externalScriptTag` containing the HTML string that links an external JavaScript file called "cipher.js".
2. Create a variable `inlineScriptTag` containing a script tag placed at the bottom of a body element.
hints: External file: <script src="cipher.js"></script>
Place scripts at the bottom of <body> so HTML loads first
External files keep your HTML clean and the JS reusable

levels.title: GATE 03 — SIGNAL BROADCAST
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

CIPHER needs to broadcast data to four different output channels simultaneously — the console, the page, a popup alert, and directly written into the document. NEXUS has jammed three of the four. Your job is to demonstrate all four output methods so the backup systems know which channel is still alive.

MISSION OBJECTIVE: Write JavaScript that uses all four output methods:
1. console.log("TRANSMITTING")
2. document.getElementById("output").innerHTML = "TRANSMITTING"
3. window.alert("TRANSMITTING")
4. document.write("TRANSMITTING")
hints: console.log() — developer console only
document.getElementById("demo").innerHTML = "text" — updates the page
window.alert("text") — popup box (use sparingly)
document.write() — overwrites the whole page if called after load, testing only

levels.title: GATE 04 — CODE STRUCTURE
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

NEXUS injected syntax errors into the training codebase. Recruits who do not understand JS syntax fundamentals are writing broken code that silently fails. Statements end with semicolons. Code blocks use curly braces. Variables are declared before use. Identifiers are case sensitive. Master the rules before the rules master you.

MISSION OBJECTIVE: Fix the broken code below. Declare two variables `x = 10` and `y = 20`, add them together into `result`, and return or log the result.
hints: Keywords are lowercase: let not Let
Statements end with ;
console.log not Console.Log
Variable names are case sensitive: x and X are different variables

levels.title: GATE 05 — CALCULATION ENGINE
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

The CIPHER targeting system runs on math. Distance calculations, threat scoring, signal strength — all of it uses operators. NEXUS corrupted the operator logic causing every calculation to return wrong results. Rebuild the calculation engine using arithmetic, assignment, and comparison operators correctly.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. Calculate the remainder of `20 % 6` and store in `remainder`.
2. Start with `let score = 100`, then use `+= 50` and `*= 2` to update it.
3. Check if `threatLevel === 73` and `threatLevel > 50`, returning `isHighThreat` boolean.
hints: % is modulo — gives the remainder: 20 % 6 returns 2
** is exponentiation: 2 ** 8 returns 256
=== is strict equality — checks value AND type, always prefer over ==

levels.title: GATE 06 — DECISION MATRIX
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

Every agent decision in the field runs through a decision matrix — a branching logic tree that evaluates conditions and picks a path. NEXUS has no decision logic — it brute forces everything. You are smarter. Build the clearance check system that routes agents to the correct access level based on their threat score.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. Write a function `evaluate(score)` that returns:
   - "CRITICAL THREAT" if score is 90 or above
   - "HIGH THREAT" if score is 70 or above
   - "MODERATE THREAT" if score is 50 or above
   - "LOW THREAT" for anything below 50
2. Write a function `missionBriefing(code)` using a switch statement that returns:
   - "OPERATION OVERLORD" for "ALPHA"
   - "OPERATION NIGHTFALL" for "BETA"
   - "OPERATION OMEGA PROTOCOL" for "OMEGA"
   - "UNKNOWN MISSION" for default.
hints: Chain conditions with else if
Order matters — check the highest value first
switch uses case "ALPHA": with break after each block
Use default: as the fallback in switch

levels.title: GATE 07 — SWEEP PROTOCOL
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

The perimeter sweep scans every node in the network one by one. Without loops, you would have to write a line of code for every single node — NEXUS has 10,000 of them. Loops let you write the logic once and repeat it as many times as needed. Automate the sweep.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. Write a function `scanNodes()` that loops through numbers 1 to 10.
2. It should skip node 4 using `continue`.
3. It should stop completely when it reaches node 7 using `break`.
4. Return the scanned nodes as an array: `[1, 2, 3, 5, 6]`.
hints: for (let i = 1; i <= 10; i++) — classic counter loop
while (i <= 10) — runs as long as condition is true, increment manually
for...of iterates array values directly
break exits the loop, continue skips to the next iteration

levels.title: GATE 08 — DECRYPTION STRINGS
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

Every intercepted NEXUS transmission is a string. To decode them you need to slice them, search them, replace words, change case, and extract characters. The decryption unit is offline. Rebuild it using JavaScript string methods.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
Given `const transmission = "  NEXUS WILL STRIKE AT MIDNIGHT ON FRIDAY  ";`:
1. `clean`: remove whitespace from both ends using `trim()`
2. `target`: replace "NEXUS" with "TARGET"
3. `hasFriday`: check if the string includes "FRIDAY"
4. `words`: split the trimmed message into an array of words
Return `{ clean, target, hasFriday, words }`.
hints: trim() removes leading and trailing whitespace
toLowerCase() / toUpperCase() change case
replace("old", "new") swaps text
includes("word") returns true or false
split(" ") breaks a string into an array by the separator

levels.title: GATE 09 — THREAT CALCULATION
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

The threat scoring system runs entirely on numbers. But numbers in JavaScript are tricky — they are all floating point, they have precision limits, and operations can produce Infinity or NaN without warning. The calculation unit needs to handle edge cases or the threat scores will be wrong and agents will be sent into danger.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. `rounded`: Round `47.6892` to 2 decimal places (as string or number)
2. `numSum`: Convert the string `"99.5"` to a number and add `0.5`
3. `maxThreat`: Find the maximum value in `44, 91, 13, 78, 55`
4. `isNexusNaN`: Check if `Number("NEXUS")` is NaN using `isNaN()`
Return `{ rounded, numSum, maxThreat, isNexusNaN }`.
hints: toFixed(2) rounds to 2 decimal places — returns a string
Number("99.5") or parseFloat("99.5") converts strings to numbers
Math.max(44, 91, 13, 78, 55) returns the highest
isNaN(Number("NEXUS")) returns true

levels.title: GATE 10 — FUNCTION FACTORY
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

CIPHER's entire operation runs on reusable functions. Without them, every agent would have to reinvent the wheel on every mission. Functions take input, process it, and return output. They are the backbone of every program ever written. Build the function factory that powers the field team.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. `greetAgent(name)`: Function returning `"Welcome back, Agent " + name`
2. `calcSignal(power, distance)`: Arrow function returning `power / distance`
3. `setAlert(level = "MEDIUM")`: Function with default parameter returning level
4. `createMultiplier(factor)`: Closure returning a function `(n) => n * factor`
Return `{ greetAgent, calcSignal, setAlert, createMultiplier }`.
hints: Declaration: function name(params) { return value; }
Arrow: const fn = (a, b) => a / b
Default param: function alert(level = "MEDIUM") {}
Closure: outer function returns (x) => x * multiplier

levels.title: GATE 11 — TIMED OPERATIONS
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

Field operations run on precise timing. The detonator countdown, the repeated status ping to HQ, the auto-logout after inactivity — all of it runs on JavaScript timers. NEXUS disrupted the timing system and now everything fires at the wrong moment. Restore the timers.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
Write a function `runCountdown(callback)` that simulates an emergency timer: it should call `setTimeout` or `setInterval` and invoke `callback("DETONATION DISARMED")`.
hints: setTimeout(fn, ms) runs once after delay
setInterval(fn, ms) runs repeatedly
Store the interval: const timer = setInterval(...)
Stop it: clearInterval(timer)

levels.title: GATE 12 — OBJECT RECONSTRUCTION
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

NEXUS shredded the agent object database. Every agent profile — their name, rank, skills, status — exists as raw scattered data. You need to reconstruct the object structure from scratch, access the data correctly, loop through its properties, and add methods that make the object do work.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
Create an `agent` object with:
- `name`: "Zero"
- `rank`: "Commander"
- `clearance`: 5
- `skills`: ["Infiltration", "Crypto"]
- `isActive`: true
- Add `missionsCompleted`: 42
- Add method `report()` returning `"Agent " + this.name + " reporting. Status: ACTIVE"`
Return `agent`.
hints: object.property — dot notation
object["property"] — bracket notation (useful with variables)
Add after: agent.newProp = value
Method: a function stored as a property, use this.name inside
for (let key in object) loops through all enumerable properties

levels.title: GATE 13 — CONTAINMENT ZONES
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

Data leaks are a critical security vulnerability. A variable that leaks out of its intended scope can expose classified information to the entire program — or to NEXUS. Understand the difference between global scope, function scope, and block scope. Contain your variables. Contain your data.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
Demonstrate scope containment. Return an object `{ globalVar, blockScopedWorks }` where:
- `globalVar` is defined outside
- In an `if (true)` block, `let blockVar = "SECURE"` cannot be leaked
- Return `{ globalVar: "CLASSIFIED", blockScopedWorks: true }`.
hints: var is function-scoped — it leaks out of if, for, etc.
let and const are block-scoped — safe inside {}
Global variables are accessible from anywhere — avoid when possible
Accessing a let variable outside its block throws ReferenceError
levels.validateCode:
if (!result || result.globalVar !== 'CLASSIFIED' || result.blockScopedWorks !== true) return { success: false, message: 'Return { globalVar: "CLASSIFIED", blockScopedWorks: true }' };
return { success: true, message: 'GATE 13 CLEARED: Containment zones sealed.' };

levels.title: GATE 14 — MISSION TIMESTAMPS
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

Every mission is logged with timestamps — when it started, when it ended, how long it lasted. The timestamp system is down. NEXUS is exploiting the gap in logs to hide its activity. Restore the date system so every operation is timestamped and traceable.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. `missionStart`: Create a Date object for `January 15, 2047 06:00:00`
2. `year`: Get the full year from missionStart
3. `month`: Get the month index (0-based) from missionStart
4. `day`: Get the day date from missionStart
Return `{ missionStart, year, month, day }`.
hints: new Date() — current date and time
new Date(2047, 0, 15, 6, 0) — month is 0-indexed (Jan = 0)
getFullYear(), getMonth(), getDate(), getHours(), getMinutes()
toDateString() gives a readable format

levels.title: GATE 15 — ARRAY ARSENAL
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

The agent roster, the target list, the equipment inventory, the intercepted coordinates — everything in CIPHER is stored in arrays. Arrays are ordered lists that let you add, remove, find, sort, and transform collections of data. Master the array arsenal and you control the data.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
Given `let agents = ["Zero", "Fox", "Rook", "Lynx", "Ghost"];`:
1. Push `"Viper"` to the end, unshift `"Echo"` to the beginning
2. Find the index of `"Rook"`
3. Sort the array alphabetically
4. Check if `"Ghost"` is included
Return `{ agents, rookIndex, hasGhost }`.
hints: push() adds to end, unshift() adds to beginning
pop() removes from end, shift() removes from beginning
indexOf("Rook") returns the position
sort() sorts array elements in place
includes("Ghost") returns true or false

levels.title: GATE 16 — UNIQUE SIGNATURES
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

NEXUS is flooding the system with duplicate signals — the same data repeated thousands of times to overwhelm the processors. A Set is a collection that only stores unique values. It automatically rejects duplicates. Use it to clean the signal stream and eliminate the noise.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. Create a Set from `[101, 202, 101, 303, 202, 404, 101, 505]`
2. Add `606` to the Set
3. Delete `202` from the Set
4. Check if `303` exists using `.has()`
5. Convert the cleaned Set back to an array named `cleanedArray`
Return `{ size: signalSet.size, has303, cleanedArray }`.
hints: new Set(array) — creates a Set and removes duplicates instantly
set.add(value) — adds a value (ignored if already exists)
set.has(value) — returns true or false
set.delete(value) — removes a specific value
[...set] or Array.from(set) — converts back to array
levels.initialCode:
const rawSignals = [101, 202, 101, 303, 202, 404, 101, 505];

// Task: Create Set, add 606, delete 202, check 303, convert to array

levels.title: GATE 17 — INTELLIGENCE MAP
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

The intelligence database needs to store key-value pairs where the keys are not simple strings — sometimes they are objects, sometimes numbers, sometimes other complex data. A regular JS object cannot handle this. A Map can. Build the intelligence Map that stores and retrieves agent data with any key type.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. Create a `new Map()`
2. Set string keys `"Zero" -> 88`, `"Fox" -> 45`, `"Rook" -> 91`
3. Set numeric badge key `1007 -> "SUPER AGENT"`
4. Get score for `"Zero"` into `zeroScore`
5. Check if badge `1007` exists using `.has(1007)`
Return `{ zeroScore, hasBadge1007: intelMap.has(1007), mapSize: intelMap.size }`.
hints: new Map() — creates an empty Map
map.set(key, value) — adds or updates an entry
map.get(key) — retrieves value by key
map.has(key) — returns true or false
map.size — total number of entries (not .length)
levels.initialCode:
const intelMap = new Map();

// Task: Store entries, numeric keys, retrieve values

levels.title: GATE 18 — ITERATION PROTOCOLS
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

Data never sits still in CIPHER. It gets looped, transformed, filtered, and reduced constantly. The iteration protocols are the engine that processes everything — from scanning the network to building reports. NEXUS cannot keep up with a developer who knows every iteration tool in the arsenal.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
Given:
`const threatData = [{ agent: "Zero", score: 88 }, { agent: "Fox", score: 45 }, { agent: "Rook", score: 91 }, { agent: "Lynx", score: 62 }, { agent: "Ghost", score: 77 }];`
1. `names`: use `map()` to extract an array of just the agent names
2. `highThreats`: use `filter()` for agents with `score > 70`
3. `totalScore`: use `reduce()` to sum all agent scores
4. `topAgent`: use `find()` for the first agent with `score > 85`
Return `{ names, highThreats, totalScore, topAgent }`.
hints: map — transforms, returns new array same length
filter — returns new array with only passing elements
reduce — collapses to single value: (acc, curr) => acc + curr.score
find — returns the first matching element (not an array)

levels.title: GATE 19 — FINAL CALCULATION
levels.story:
[INCOMING TRANSMISSION — CIPHER HQ]

This is the final gate. NEXUS runs a mathematical defense system — a series of calculations that determines whether to open the kill switch port. You need to solve each calculation correctly using the JavaScript Math object. Get one wrong and the port locks forever. There is no margin for error. This is what you trained for.

MISSION OBJECTIVE:
1. `floorVal`: Math.floor(84.4)
2. `ceilVal`: Math.ceil(84.5)
3. `absVal`: Math.abs(-273)
4. `powerVal`: Math.pow(2, 32)
5. `sqrtVal`: Math.sqrt(1764)
6. `minVal`: Math.min(33, 11, 78, 5, 92, 44)
7. `piFixed`: (Math.PI).toFixed(4)
Return `{ floorVal, ceilVal, absVal, powerVal, sqrtVal, minVal, piFixed }`.
hints: Math.floor() rounds down, Math.ceil() rounds up, Math.round() rounds to nearest
Math.abs(-273) returns 273
Math.pow(2, 32) or 2 ** 32
Math.sqrt(1764) returns 42
Math.PI is the constant 3.14159...
(Math.PI).toFixed(4) returns "3.1416"
